one_liner: Cython UAX #29 grapheme splitter for CPython; about 8x faster than ICU's BreakIterator driven through PyICU on a short string.
what_it_does: Splits Python str objects into Unicode 16.0 extended grapheme clusters. It offers allocation-free standalone functions (grapheme_split, grapheme_len, grapheme_at, grapheme_slice, grapheme_iter, grapheme_offsets) and a str-like graphemes type that indexes, slices, finds, replaces, joins, hashes and pickles by grapheme, with terminal-width ljust/rjust/center through uwcwidth. It is not a drop-in for ICU's BreakIterator: it takes and returns Python str rather than boundary offsets in UTF-16 code units, and offers no word, line or sentence segmentation.
how_it_is_fast: Grapheme_Cluster_Break, InCB and Extended_Pictographic properties are stored as two-level sparse bitmaps, under 11 KB in total, so a lookup is two loads plus shifts after an unsigned range compare. The UAX #29 rules are a small hand-written state machine over (state, current, next) code points with an early exit for any pair below U+0300. Separate loops read CPython's PEP 393 1-, 2- and 4-byte string storage in place, so nothing is decoded or copied (Latin-1 strings only test for CR LF), and output slices are built straight from that buffer with PyUnicode_FromKindAndData.
when_to_use: CPython code that needs user-perceived character counts, indexing, truncation or reversal of emoji, Indic conjunct, Hangul or flag text.
Hot paths over many short strings (chat messages, UI labels, terminal cells), where ICU via PyICU loses most of its time to binding calls and UnicodeString conversion.
Replacing the pure-Python grapheme or uniseg packages, which the README shows splitting the Devanagari conjunct च्छे wrongly and running 43-52x slower.
Cython projects that can cimport the provided .pxd files for typed grapheme operations without Python-call overhead.
Long text: in this session grapheme_split did 31,000 mixed code points in about 0.37 ms, and grapheme_len did ASCII at about 4 GB/s (Xeon VM, Python 3.11, indicative only).
when_not_to_use: C or C++ code: this is a CPython-only extension, and the segmentation core is Cython cdef functions with no C API.
Word, line or sentence breaking, locale tailoring, or Unicode 17 tables: it implements only extended grapheme clusters at Unicode 16.0 and has had no commits since 2024-10-28.
Code that multiplies graphemes objects (g * n): replication builds a wrong grapheme index in common edge cases (see gotchas).
Platforms without a published wheel (CPython 3.14+, Linux aarch64, PyPy): pip has to build from the sdist with Cython and a C compiler.
When you need the Python-side table generator: the generation scripts are not in the repository (issue #2, open since October 2024).

integration.dependencies: uwcwidth (runtime); Cython, setuptools and a C compiler only when building from source
integration.min_toolchain: CPython 3.8+ (0.8 wheels cover cp38-cp313 for manylinux x86-64/i686, musllinux, macOS arm64 and Windows; built with -O3 on non-MSVC compilers)
integration.platforms: CPython only; prebuilt wheels for x86-64 and i686 Linux, Windows and macOS arm64; other targets build from the sdist
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The standalone functions keep no mutable state and run while holding the GIL (no nogil sections); graphemes objects are immutable values (+= returns a new object). The module keeps a static cache of single-character Latin-1 strings that is filled at init time, and free-threaded CPython is not addressed.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it replaces the README's PyICU BreakIterator generator one-for-one for grapheme splitting of Python strings, but it has no BreakIterator API, no other boundary types, no locales and no UTF-16 offsets

gotchas: Correctness bug in replication (graphemes.__mul__), reproduced in this session with the PyPI 0.8 wheel; grapheme_split, grapheme_len, the constructor and + all agreed with each other in a 100,000-case fuzz. First, grapheme_calc_tran checks `upos >= len - upos` instead of `upos >= len`, so when the last grapheme starts in the second half of the string it returns state 0 and the seam check is skipped: len(graphemes('कखक्') * 2) is 6, but grapheme_len('कखक्' * 2) is 5. Second, the slow path for count >= 3 assumes every seam merges the same way, so len(graphemes('🇭') * 4) is 1 and iteration yields only '🇭🇭' although str() holds all four. About 10% of random short strings gave a wrong list(g * 3); tests/test_graphemes.py covers replication only for CR LF and a split ZWJ emoji.
Slicing a graphemes object returns a plain str, so further slicing counts code points again (README gotcha; also the cause of closed issue #5). Use gslice to stay in graphemes.

Negative positions are inconsistent (open issue #7): grapheme_slice clamps a negative start to 0, so grapheme_slice('abcdef', -2) returns 'abcdef', while graphemes('abcdef').gslice(-2) returns 'ef'; grapheme_at returns '' for negative positions.

graphemes objects are limited to 4,294,967,294 code points and add about 4 bytes per character for the offset table; the standalone grapheme_* functions have no length limit and do not allocate an index.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when the caller is CPython. uni-algo and libutf are the catalogued choices for native C/C++ grapheme breaking against ICU4C, and fast-grapheme-segmenter (Rust) and unicode-segmenter (JavaScript) cover their own runtimes. The jquast wcwidth package (0.9.1) now ships iter_graphemes too, but it ran about 55x slower than grapheme_split on the README string in this session.
verified_claims_summary: First-party IPython %%timeit means on one 15-cluster string: grapheme_split 337 ns against 2.84 us for ICU's character BreakIterator called through PyICU from a Python generator that converts to icu.UnicodeString and builds one str per cluster (8.4x), and against 8.19 us for pyuegc, 14.6 us for uniseg and 17.4 us for grapheme (the last two split wrongly). No CPU, OS or Python/PyICU/ICU versions are stated and there is no benchmark script, so the 8.4x is mostly binding overhead on a tiny input rather than ICU's C++ segmentation. In this session, on an Intel Xeon 2.1 GHz cloud VM with Python 3.11.15 and the 0.8 wheel, the same call took about 417 ns (best of 7) and passed all 1,093 Unicode 16.0 GraphemeBreakTest cases; PyICU was not installed, so the ICU ratio was not re-measured.
status_note: Stale (last commit and release 0.8 on 2024-10-28, 40 stars, four open issues including the negative-slicing report #7), but 0BSD-licensed with wheels up to CPython 3.13; safe for the standalone split, length and slice functions, while g * n should be avoided until the replication bug is fixed.
